title: The paper rocket
summary: Every one of Dani's paper rockets nosedives. Until number twelve, which one night doesn't come down.

scenes.text:
Dani was five years old and wanted to go to space.

Not when he was grown up. Now.

So that afternoon he tore a page out of his notebook, laid it on the table, and folded it.

In half. The corners in. In half again. With his tongue poking out from trying so hard.

It came out a slightly wonky rocket. He threw it from the bed and it went nose-first into the floor.

He made another. It fell.

He made another one. It fell on the cat, who walked off deeply offended.

"Paper rockets don't go to space," his sister said from the doorway.

Dani didn't answer. He was already tearing out another page.

Rocket number twelve came out perfect.

It had a sharp nose, matching wings and a little window drawn in blue pencil. Dani hid it under his pillow and waited for night.

When everyone was asleep, he opened the window.

The air smelled of night. Down below, the street was empty and the streetlamps made yellow circles on the ground.

Dani held the rocket up in both hands, aimed it at the sky and counted very softly:

"Three. Two. One."

And with all his might, he launched it.

The rocket climbed. It passed the roof across the street. It passed the aerial. It passed the lowest cloud.

And it didn't come down.

Dani never found out how it happened, because things like that happen without warning.

One moment he was at the window, and the next he was riding the rocket, holding on to its nose, his pyjamas flapping like a flag.

Up and up they went. The city shrank to a board covered in tiny lights. Then the clouds. Then nothing but the huge black sky, full of points of light.

They passed so close to the moon that Dani could see its craters.

And then, a little further on, he heard someone crying.

It was a yellow star. Small, round, and so dim you could hardly see it.

"Why are you crying?" asked Dani.

"Because I'm the smallest in the sky," said the star. "Nobody on Earth can see me. Everyone looks at the moon, or at the big stars. Nobody has ever looked at me."

Dani thought about it.

"I'll look at you," he said. "Every night."

"You won't find me. I'm too small."

"Yes I will," said Dani, and he studied carefully where she was. "To the left of the moon. A little bit lower. Next to three stars that make a triangle."

The star stopped crying. And, little by little, she began to shine.

Dani woke up in his own bed, tucked in up to his nose.

Rocket number twelve was on his bedside table, a little crumpled, as if it had been on a very long journey.

Dani got up and went to the window.

He found the moon. To the left. A little bit lower. Next to three stars that made a triangle.

There she was. Small, round, yellow.

And when Dani looked at her, she gave him a wink.
